A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FinFRE-RAG fraud-detection study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fraud-detection experiments, ablations, fine-tuning comparisons and qualitative analyses in Section 4, plus measured inference efficiency in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including detection scores, ablations and appendix latency and token measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical Random Forest feature selection, categorical filtering, cosine-similarity retrieval and prompt-based risk scoring. No algorithm, model component or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use CCF, CCFRAUD, IEEE-CIS and PAYSIM for the same fraud-detection tasks, including the same CCFRAUD and IEEE-CIS fine-tuning comparison.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain identical: direct-prompted LLMs, Random Forest, XGBoost and TabM in Table 1, and the same three fine-tuned LLMs in Table 4.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A-D retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations and training budgets, including 8,000 test transactions, 2,000 validation transactions and default k=10 and n=20.

E4.justification: Feature and retrieval-count sensitivity tests, random-feature ablation, scoring-versus-binary comparison, behavioral case study and efficiency analysis are unchanged in Figures 2-4, Tables 2-3 and Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging three runs in Section 4.1. Run-count information and uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged; no seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests are added.

E6.justification: All reported scores, plotted results, example responses and appendix efficiency measurements are identical. For example, Table 1 retains CCF F1=0.31 and MCC=0.36 for Qwen3-14B with FinFRE-RAG.

T1.justification: The problem definitions and normalization, categorical-filtering and cosine-similarity equations in Section 3 are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about adapting LLMs through feature reduction and retrieval, improving over direct prompting and supporting interpretable fraud analysis.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications remain identical, including explanations of model behavior, retrieval-label bias, noncausal rationales, public-dataset limitations and the Appendix A warning about PAYSIM leakage.

D1.justification: Hardware, hyperparameters, tuning procedures, prompts, dataset access information and efficiency-measurement details remain unchanged in Section 4.1 and Appendices A-D. The added funding acknowledgement supplies no technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tan, Hu and Zhang (2026), 'Benchmarking bias mitigation toward fairness without harm from vision to LVLMs,' to the introductory background citations and bibliography. Research positioning otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgements section listing NSF funding awards, inserts one introductory citation and updates the arXiv version/date text. The scientific prose and existing section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement and added reference cause limited reflow of the bibliography across pages 9-12, with small introductory line-wrap changes. All figures, tables and appendix layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding attribution and one background citation, providing modest disclosure and bibliographic context. The method, empirical evidence, claims, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged, and the layout changes are limited. These additions do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
